transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-15
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen, Miguel Alvarez, Priya Rao, Jesse Kim, Nina Park, Omar El-Sayed + company-wide

[00:00] Host - Laura Chen: Hey everyone, welcome to the October leadership update, um, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: Q3 recap, product + infra, hiring, security, customer highlights, and then q&a. We'll try to keep it tight, okay?

[00:28] Laura Chen: First, quick house keeping - recording's on, please keep questions for the Q&A section or drop them in chat.

[00:45] Miguel Alvarez: Alright jumping into Q3, some high level numbers — revenue came in a bit ahead of our internal plan, ARR growth at about 28% quarter over quarter, churn improved slightly, and usage on Dedicated continues to ramp. A couple caveats — mix shifted towards smaller dedicated deals, which affects near-term ACV but improves adoption footprint.

[01:22] Nina Park: To add, sales pipeline is healthy, pipeline coverage is at 3.2x for Q4; biggest closed enterprise wins were in finserv and healthcare — both required our Private offering with stricter controls.

[01:54] Host - Laura Chen: Great. Priya, product?

[02:02] Priya Rao: Yep, product updates. We shipped the streaming improvements and improved batching heuristics in late September; customers are seeing 12–20% latency reductions for chat workloads, and token cost savings from smarter KV cache reuse is material. Note: some early customers reported minor regressions in safety filters after the streaming change — we've patched two rule sets and will push a more robust eval this week.

[02:42] Jesse Kim: On the infra side, the runtime now supports better kernel selection for Llama2-like models and several optimized paths for quantized variants. We validated on A100 and H100 clusters; results look promising. There's a note though — our autoscaler had a blipping issue during a big demo last week where burst capacity didn't kick in immediately, that's resolved by a hotfix.

[03:18] Employee (scattered): There was a question in chat about Dedicated vs Hosted — what guidance are we giving?

[03:28] Nina Park: Short answer: Hosted for rapid PLG adoption and lowest time-to-value; Dedicated when customers need throughput guarantees and data isolation; Private for regulatory/air-gapped needs. Sales playbooks have been updated — link in the follow-up.

[03:52] Miguel Alvarez: Also added: smart routing improvements can now fallback to compatible quantized variants when capacity constraints hit — helps maintain availability without a full model downgrade.

[04:20] Laura Chen: Good. On the product roadmap — Priya high-level Q4 priorities?

[04:29] Priya Rao: Q4 priorities: 1) Improve Private deployment onboarding (reduce time-to-first-inference), 2) Launch model pinning & rollout UI in Console, 3) More observability for per-route cost and token-level traces, 4) Expand curated model catalog with 2 new open models tested for inference economics. Expect a phased rollout Nov–Dec.

[05:03] Priya Rao: Quick callout on model pinning — customers asked for easier canarying. The plan is canary by percentage + automatic fallback policy (by latency SLO). Implementation in console and api coming in November.

[05:30] Laura Chen: Thanks. Hiring and org changes — Jesse?

[05:36] Jesse Kim: Engineering hiring — we're opening 18 new IC roles across runtime, infra and dev-ex by EOY. We're also promoting two leads: Sara V. to Head of Runtime and Arman S. to Principal Infra. That should help with ownership for Dedicated autoscaling and the Private install flow.

[06:05] People Ops (Laura reading): We're prioritizing diverse sourcing and expect interview loops to be updated. Timeline for new hires — first cohort interviews start next week.

[06:28] Laura Chen: Security update — Omar?

[06:33] Omar El-Sayed: Security, compliance progress: SOC 2 Type II audit scheduled for early December, we've closed 9 of 12 high-priority controls from the audit prep list. KMS integration with major cloud providers is complete in Private, and we're testing HSM flows for on-prem. Also implemented more granular RBAC in Console. Note: retention policy questions — will share updated doc.

[07:04] Employee (someone muttering): Any data residency plans?

[07:09] Omar El-Sayed: Yes, regional deployments roadmap going into Q1; we'll support EU and APAC regions with localized storage options and customer-managed keys.

[07:28] Laura Chen: Customer highlights — Nina?

[07:32] Nina Park: Highlight a couple wins: HealthCo (pseudonym) completed a Private pilot and moved to production for clinical summarization, SecurBank expanded Dedicated contract and asked for deeper latency SLAs. We also saw a large PLG account spike after we rolled out the streaming perf improvements. Case studies to follow.

[07:58] Laura Chen: Cool. Any product-market fit learnings?

[08:03] Priya Rao: We're seeing jobs around structured output and reranking — customers building retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines want predictable latency for short queries; that maps well to our Dedicated + cache features. Also customers want simpler quantization profiles out-of-the-box.

[08:28] Employee question (Jon): What's happening with pricing for Dedicated?

[08:35] Nina Park: We're testing a pilot where Dedicated has a base commit + consumption for burst; pricing details TBD — we want to balance unit economics and the customer's desire for predictability. We'll run a small set of pilot customers and iterate.

[09:01] Laura Chen: Alright we'll open for Q&A. Please unmute in order; we'll take raised hands first.

[09:10] [09:10] Anonymous (IC): What are the biggest risks for Q4?

[09:15] Miguel Alvarez: Risk 1: performance regressions from complex streaming changes — mitigations: more evals and staged rollouts; Risk 2: hiring slippage — mitigations: prioritize key roles; Risk 3: cloud capacity variance affecting burst — mitigations: stronger fallback policies and multi-region pools.

[09:53] [09:53] Anonymous (IC): Any updates on the autoscaling incident?

[09:57] Jesse Kim: Root cause was a race in the scheduler under high concurrency; we released a hotfix that adds backpressure and a circuit-breaker for the burst path. We've scheduled a load test next week to validate at scale.

[10:24] [10:24] Anonymous (PM): Can we get more clarity on rollout controls in the Console?

[10:30] Priya Rao: The Console rollout will allow pin-by-version, canary by percentage, and auto-fallback based on latency or error thresholds. We're adding a visual timeline and audit log entries per rollout step.

[11:00] [11:00] Employee: Is there any change to our open model curation policy?

[11:05] Priya Rao: Slight tweak — models will need a validated perf profile (latency/cost/regression tests) plus safety/eval pass before being listed as "Redwood-verified" in the catalog.

[11:35] [11:35] Anonymous (Sales): For the customer demo last week, some of the numbers in the deck didn't match the live benchmark sheet, is there a canonical source?

[11:44] Miguel Alvarez: Yes canonical is the perf spreadsheet in the infra drive; I'll re-share link and lock versioning. Also note: some model names were transcribed wrong in the deck (Llama -> Llama2-xl etc.) — be careful.

[12:10] [12:10] Laura Chen: Quick product/marketing ask — can we get top 3 metrics we want to show in sales decks?

[12:18] Nina Park: Top 3: median latency at 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens vs baseline, and successful canary rate (no regressions on evals).

[12:40] [12:40] Anonymous (IC): Are we open to partnering with cloud vendors on managed endpoints?

[12:45] Laura Chen: We are exploring partnerships but want to keep the core runtime differentiation strong; potential channel plays are possible but not primary focus.

[13:05] [13:05] Employee: Any changes to OKRs?

[13:09] Laura Chen: Minor adjustments — more weight on stability metrics and customer onboarding speed. We'll share updated OKR doc later today.

[13:30] Priya Rao: Small demo note — the model pinning UI will have an API equivalent so platform teams can automate rollouts.

[13:48] Jesse Kim: On infra infra cost optimization, the Optimize team's proposals include smarter packing and preemptible-friendly scheduling for non-critical workloads; we estimate ~8–12% infra cost savings if we land it.

[14:22] [14:22] Employee (Finance): Revenue recognition question — are we changing contract terms that affect revenue timing?

[14:27] Nina Park: No major change; some pilots may move earlier to consumption-first pricing but we'll coordinate with finance.

[14:50] [14:50] Anonymous (IC): Any note on model updates — how do we handle breaking changes?

[14:55] Priya Rao: We'll use the pinned rollout flow and ensure compatibility tests run as part of the deployment gating; plus notify customers with a 2-week notice for major model architecture changes.

[15:20] [15:20] Laura Chen: Ok wrapping up — quick recap of commitments. Priya to share roadmap, Miguel to share perf sheet, People Ops to share hiring timeline, CS to surface case studies. Links and slide deck will be in the follow-up email.

[15:44] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone, commitment to focus on stability and onboarding speed — see you at the next update. Meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcription quality: filler words and occasional misheard proper nouns (e.g., H100/H700 mis-typed in earlier notes), speaker labels auto-attributed in some places.
